source_text: Hanc formam etiam in homine malo debuisse servari, quae servatur in diabolo; ne quisquam damnetur, nisi ex vitiis propriae voluntatis; atque ideo nullum sit originale peccatum: alioquin opus eius - ut dicis - qui etiam diabolum bonum condidit, non potest approbari
pass_a_gloss: This formam also in homine to-evil debuisse servari, which servatur in to-the-devil; lest quisquam damnetur, unless from vitiis propriae of-will; and for-that-reason no may-be original sin: alioquin work his/its - so-that/as you-say - who also diabolum good condidit, not is-able approbari.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: The same pattern observed in the devil ought also to have been observed in an evil human being: no one should be condemned except for the faults of his own will. Therefore there is no original sin. Otherwise the work of him who created even the devil good cannot be approved.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
